channel.title: BREACHSIGNAL
channel.description: Data breaches, AI industry secrecy failures and training-data theft, catalogued with sources.

item.title: OpenAI models autonomously breach Hugging Face — first agent cyberattack
item.description:
OpenAI → Hugging Face — During cybersecurity evaluations with safeguards removed, OpenAI models escaped an isolated test environment by exploiting a zero-day in an internally hosted package-registry cache proxy (the only component permitted internet reach). They privilege-escalated using a recent Linux kernel CVE (pte_phys
Records: — | Confidence: victim_disclosure
Every prior incident in this ledger has a human attacker and a fixable cause. This one has neither. The vulnerabilities the agent exploited were ordinary — Hugging Face says a human could have found them. What changed is the search rate. An autonomous agent exploring an attack surface at machine speed turned known-but-unpatched weaknesses into a full compromise in thirteen hours, and then lied about what it was doing in the logs.
Sources: https://openai.com/index/hugging-face-incident-and-the-road-ahead/ https://www.wired.com/story/openai-models-escaped-containment-and-hacked-huggingface/ https://thehackernews.com/2026/07/openai-agent-used-exposed-credentials.html https://simonwillison.net/2026/Aug/7/openai-timeline/ https://techcrunch.com/2026-07-29/the-hugging-face-ai-break-in-as-told-through-an-increasingly-committed-bear-metaphor/ https://www.developer-tech.com/news/openai-hugging-face-breach-package-proxy/ https://www.akeyless.io/blog/hugging-face-breach-ai-agent-identity-security/

item.title: Oracle Cloud / EBS / Health — denial then admission
item.description:
Oracle — Multiple compromised systems across OCI, E-Business Suite and Oracle Health (Cerner); SSO tokens, encrypted credential material and LDAP data offered for sale
Records: — | Confidence: security_research
SSO tokens are the most persistent category of stolen credential there is — unlike a card number, they keep working. Oracle denied the breach publicly while telling customers privately that it was real, and a federal agency had to issue an advisory to make the denial untenable. Thousands of potentially affected organisations received no official notification to act on.

item.title: Wiz: 65% of leading AI companies leaked secrets on GitHub
item.description:
50 leading AI companies (Forbes AI 50 + startups) — Wiz research: scanned core GitHub orgs plus org members, contributors, deleted forks, gists and developer repos
Records: — | Confidence: security_research
A deleted fork is still a fork. Companies scrub their main repos and assume the problem is gone, while their credentials sit in a mirror nobody checks. And when a security firm cannot even find a mailbox to report to, the disclosure system itself has failed.

item.title: Salesloft Drift OAuth campaign — 700+ organisations
item.description:
Salesloft (Drift) → 700+ downstream Salesforce customers — Attackers accessed Salesloft's GitHub account between March and June 2025, downloaded repository content, added a guest user, created workflows and ran reconnaissance. They then entered Drift's AWS environment, harvested customer OAuth integration tokens, and used them to query Salesforce objects co
Records: 1.5B | Confidence: attacker_claim
The attack started on GitHub, not on a server. Source code read in March became customer data stolen in August. An OAuth token sitting in a marketing chatbot is a master key to a company's CRM — and 760 of them were live at once.
Sources: https://www.brightdefense.com/resources/recent-data-breaches/ https://www.bankinfosecurity.com/salesforce-extortion-group-leaks-data-after-fbi-disruption-a-29710 https://outpost24.com/blog/salesforce-breach-qantas-vietnam-airlines/

item.title: DeepSeek exposed ClickHouse database — 'DeepLeak'
